data.title: Nvidia Launches Three Nemotron AI Models, Including Two for Local AI Agents
data.ai_summary: Nvidia launched three Nemotron AI models, including the 120-billion-parameter Super VL and two smaller Bolt models for local AI agents. The models are available through Hugging Face, OpenRouter, and Nvidia's NIM, with the Bolt 74B-A9B requiring 24GB memory and the Bolt E4B needing 4GB. Early adopters include Scale AI and EY.
data.author: Aminu Abdullahi
data.full_text:
Nvidia wants AI agents to handle more complex work without requiring every task to run through a massive cloud-hosted model.

The company has introduced three Nemotron models, led by the 120-billion-parameter Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, which can analyze documents, interpret images, and use external tools to complete multistep tasks. Two smaller Bolt models are designed to bring similar agent capabilities to compatible PCs and edge devices.

Unlike models focused primarily on text generation, Super VL can extract information from PDFs, interpret charts and tables, and use tools to execute multistep workflows. That combination could help automate document-heavy work in finance, cybersecurity, engineering and research.

The model is available through Hugging Face, OpenRouter, ModelScope and Nvidia’s NIM deployment platform. Organizations can also fine-tune it using proprietary data, tools and policies.

Two smaller models bring agents closer to users

Nvidia also introduced two Nemotron 3.5 Bolt models designed to run AI agents locally. The Bolt 74B-A9B uses 2-bit quantization, a compression technique that reduces the memory needed to store model weights. Nvidia says this allows the 74-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model, which activates about nine billion parameters at a time, to fit within a 24GB memory footprint.

The model targets local research, web browsing, coding, and debugging on compatible Nvidia RTX and DGX systems.

The model is available now through Hugging Face, with support for tools including Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp and vLLM.

The smaller Bolt E4B requires 4GB of memory and targets conversational agents, voice assistants, interactive characters and physical AI applications. It is designed for GeForce RTX, Jetson and RTX/DGX Spark hardware, with release scheduled for Oct. 23.

Together, the three models give developers options for deploying agents across different computing environments rather than relying exclusively on remote AI services.

Advertisement

Open models give enterprises more control

Nvidia trained Super VL on about 26 trillion tokens, then post-trained it on about 3.8 million samples, followed by reinforcement learning across dozens of environments. The company is releasing model weights, datasets and training recipes to support customization.

Early adopters include Scale AI, which post-trained the model for Skydance’s vendor credit finance agent and EY’s merger-and-acquisition due diligence agent. Other organizations are adapting it for cybersecurity, financial document analysis, coding and medical claims processing.

Nvidia also says its Dynamo serving platform can support up to eight times as many users while reducing latency by 85% under specified deployment conditions.

Local AI still depends on hardware

The Bolt models could make private, locally run agents more practical for developers and businesses handling sensitive information. Keeping workloads on compatible hardware can reduce dependence on cloud services, though privacy still depends on system configuration, application permissions and how connected tools handle data.

The 24GB model’s compressed format also comes with an important caveat: fitting a model into memory does not automatically guarantee the best accuracy or responsiveness for every task. Businesses will need to test reliability, speed and resource use against their own workloads before deploying agents at scale.

Advertisement

More must-read AI coverage

What Nvidia’s new models mean for developers and businesses

The Bolt models could make locally run AI agents more practical for developers and businesses that want greater control over their workloads. Running models on compatible hardware can reduce dependence on cloud services, although privacy still depends on system configuration, application permissions, and how connected tools handle data.

For developers, Bolt could support coding assistants and research agents that operate on a compatible PC without sending every request to a cloud provider. Meanwhile, Super VL offers businesses another option for building specialized agents around internal documents and workflows.

However, smaller memory requirements do not automatically guarantee better performance. Organizations will still need to evaluate model accuracy, responsiveness, hardware compatibility, and resource use before deploying these systems at scale.

Consumers may eventually encounter smaller models in local voice assistants, interactive game characters, and device interfaces. But the immediate significance of Nvidia’s launch is the broader range of hardware and deployment options available to developers building AI agents.

Other news: Nvidia has made its entire Run:ai GPU orchestration platform open source, allowing organizations to manage GPU resources and AI workloads on Kubernetes without a software subscription.

data.title: Nvidia launches Nemotron 3.5 Super VL and Bolt for AI agents
data.ai_summary: Nvidia released three open models for AI agents: Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, a 120B-parameter multimodal model, and two Bolt models for local hardware. Super VL achieves up to five times higher throughput than its class runner-up, while Bolt 74B-A9B fits into 24GB memory. The models are available on Hugging Face and other platforms.
data.author: Berry Zwets
data.full_text: Nvidia is releasing three new open models for AI agents. Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is a multimodal model with 120 billion parameters designed for enterprise workloads. It is also releasing two Bolt models that run locally on RTX and DGX Spark hardware. With these three models, Nvidia aims to cover every layer of agent deployments: from large enterprise servers to edge devices and local hardware. Organizations running agents on Nvidia infrastructure will thus have an open model for every level. Super VL was developed in collaboration with the Nemotron Coalition. According to Nvidia, the model achieves accuracy comparable to the company’s largest reasoning model for multimodal agent tasks (following instructions, using tools, multi-step business processes, and visual understanding), with about one-fifth the parameters. Speed is the other key selling point. On the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, Super VL achieves up to five times higher throughput than the runner-up in its class. According to Nvidia, when the model runs on Nvidia Dynamo, organizations can serve up to eight times more users with 85 percent lower latency. The visual component focuses on what agents encounter in practice: OCR, tables, charts, web pages, and PDFs. Because a single model combines text and images, tasks don’t need to be transferred between separate systems. The model was trained on approximately 26 trillion tokens and then refined using about 3.8 million samples and reinforcement learning. The model comes with open weights, datasets, and training recipes. Super VL is available on Hugging Face, OpenRouter, and ModelScope, and is offered as a NIM microservice updated every two weeks. Bolt runs locally Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB uses native 2-bit quantization and therefore fits into 24GB of memory, alongside other applications. According to Nvidia, the model is the best open-source model in its class on PinchBench and ranks second on BrowseComp. Support for llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio, Unsloth, and vLLM is available out of the box. The model is built for the RTX Spark laptops launching today. Bolt E4B 4GB targets voice assistants, interactive characters, and embedded interfaces on GeForce RTX, Jetson, and DGX Spark. Dozens of organizations are now training Super VL on their own data. Atlassian uses it for agentic search in Jira and Confluence, while CrowdStrike uses it for agentic blue teaming. Dassault Systèmes, Perplexity, Salesforce, and Synopsys are also integrating the model. Scale AI adapted it for an EY due diligence agent. TrainLoop trained it using dermatology data from Nolla. Super VL and Bolt 74B-A9B are available immediately; Bolt E4B will follow on October 23. Tip: Nvidia is building Nemotron 4 with at least 1 trillion parameters

data.author: Joseph Gabriel Lagonsin

industries.name: Agents & Autonomous Workflows (Tool Use, Planning, Multi-Agent)

data.full_text:
JOSEPH GABRIEL LAGONSIN News Editor

Nvidia has released Nemotron 3.5 Super VL and two new Nemotron 3.5 Bolt models, expanding its open model range for AI agents across servers, desktop systems and edge devices. Super VL is a 120-billion-parameter open model aimed at specialised always-on agents. Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB and Bolt E4B 4GB target smaller local and edge deployments. Super VL and Bolt 74B-A9B are available now, while Bolt E4B will follow later. The release extends Nvidia's Nemotron family, which also includes Lightning and Ultra. Nvidia positions Lightning for high-throughput workloads, Ultra for more demanding reasoning tasks and Bolt for edge use. Model range Super VL is designed for multimodal agent tasks such as instruction following, tool use, multistep business workflows and visual understanding. Nvidia says it delivers accuracy comparable with its largest reasoning model at about one-fifth of the parameter count. Nvidia also describes Super VL as the fastest open agentic model in its class, citing throughput of up to five times that of rivals on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index leaderboard. The model is open for post-training on proprietary data and can be deployed on an organisation's own infrastructure. Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB is designed for local workloads on Nvidia RTX and DGX Spark systems. It uses native 2-bit quantisation to fit into 24GB of memory, allowing it to run alongside other applications on local hardware. The model is intended for tasks such as web research, writing and debugging code without sending workloads to cloud services. Nvidia cites rankings of first among open models in its class on PinchBench and second among open models on BrowseComp. Bolt E4B 4GB is aimed at physical and conversational agents running on GeForce RTX, Jetson and RTX or DGX Spark devices. It is designed for local voice assistants, interactive characters and embedded interfaces. Customisation push Dozens of organisations are post-training Super VL with their own data, tools, policies and workflows, according to Nvidia. The company identified users across finance, cybersecurity, software development, healthcare and scientific research. Scale AI has post-trained the model for Skydance's vendor credit finance agent and for EY's M&A due diligence agent. AfterQuery customised the model for Hebbia for credit agreement analysis, while AI21 and Alice post-trained it for cybersecurity attack resilience. Mercor has used the model on the APEX-SWE coding benchmark for coding agents that plan, write and debug software. ModelScope supports fine-tuning through its ms-swift framework for specialised multimodal applications. Other organisations named by Nvidia include Ramp for financial document intelligence, Dream for cybersecurity research and vulnerability analysis, Lila Sciences for scientific discovery and search, and R1 for medical claims analysis and revenue cycle management. TrainLoop post-trained the model with dermatology data from Nolla. Software platform groups integrating Super VL include Atlassian for agentic search across products such as Jira and Confluence, CrowdStrike for enterprise security work, Dassault Systèmes for engineering design and simulation, Perplexity for search tasks, Salesforce for government workflow automation, and Synopsys for semiconductor design verification interoperability. Vision and control The model's visual strengths focus on common business documents and interfaces, including optical character recognition, tables, charts and other structured information, Nvidia says. It can process webpages, PDFs and images, extract text and return results based on the information it finds. Nvidia says its open approach is intended to give users more control over data handling, security and deployment. Super VL ships with open weights, datasets and training recipes, and organisations can run it wherever their security and data residency requirements demand. In practical terms, the model can be adapted for uses such as fraud review in insurance and credit assessment in financial services while keeping systems on premises. Customisation is supported through Nvidia NeMo, Python-based pipelines and open datasets. Super VL was trained on about 26 trillion tokens across pretraining and continued pretraining, then post-trained with roughly 3.8 million samples and reinforcement learning across dozens of environments. Nvidia is also releasing open datasets covering tool use, finance, instruction following, long context, fairness and vision-language understanding, along with reinforcement learning environments in NeMo Gym. Nvidia says the model can run across its hardware range, including DGX Spark, DGX Station, RTX Pro and RTX systems, Jetson platforms, and data centre and cloud environments. Bolt 74B-A9B is also available with support for software including llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio, Unsloth and vLLM. The three models are intended to cover deployments from large enterprise servers to local hardware and edge devices, giving organisations an open model option for each infrastructure tier.

Open models offer more control NVIDIA is releasing Super VL with open weights and supporting training materials. Its training process covered approximately 26 trillion tokens. Local deployment also gives them greater control over sensitive information, depending on their infrastructure and configuration.

data.title: Cómo es trabajar de entrenar y evaluar a una IA
data.ai_summary: A study by DiPLab and Reversing.Works found that European Outlier workers earn an average of €1,214 monthly, with 70-100% of their income from the platform. The platform collects personal data and tracks activity, and the authors believe it violates current EU regulations.
data.full_text: La inteligencia artificial parece muy lista, pero no aprende sola. Miles de humanos han guiado su aprendizaje, corrigiendo y ajustando sus respuestas. Un informe publicado este jueves por las plataformas de investigación DiPLab y Reversing.Works da nuevos detalles sobre cómo miles de trabajadores europeos trabajan a ratos sueltos para Outlier, una plataforma de Scale AI. En junio de 2025, Meta pagó 12.400 millones de euros por el 49% de Scale AI y su fundador, Alexandr Wang, pasó a ser director de IA de la compañía de Mark Zuckerberg. Antes de esa adquisición, Outlier ayudaba también a entrenar los modelos de empresas como OpenAI o Google. Según el informe, la mayoría de quienes entrenan a la IA en Europa son jóvenes formados, pero que viven en condiciones precarias. Más de la mitad son menores de 30 años y casi todos tienen un título de grado o máster. Su salario medio en la plataforma es de 1214 euros al mes. Muchos dependen de ella para vivir, según el informe, de la que obtienen entre el 70% y el 100% de sus ingresos. Los ingresos dependen de la diferencia entre tareas y la dedicación: hay colaboradores que llegan a ingresar más de 4000 euros mensuales y otros que apenas sacan 100 euros. Qué hacen los evaluadores de IA La labor de estos colaboradores varía, pero es básicamente valorar las respuestas de un chatbot con una nota: “Ayudarás a entrenar un chatbot de IA”, dicen las instrucciones generales de Outlier. “Para ello, leerás el historial de una conversación, evaluarás las respuestas que dos modelos distintos han dado a la misma instrucción, determinarás cuál de las dos responde mejor y, después, justificarás por qué es mejor”. Las tareas también pueden ser escribir textos modelo o describir imágenes. Antes de la IA, estas tareas sencillas y mecánicas se pagaban en céntimos. Ahora se ha sofisticado ligeramente y se paga algo mejor. Según su propia página, Outlier tiene más de 900.000 “expertos” registrados en 52 países a quienes han pagado más de 600 millones de dólares. “Yo lo último que he hecho han sido tareas de matemáticas, pero también he hecho tareas de programación y de español, y el formato puede cambiar”, dice un matemático y colaborador español de Outlier, que prefiere no revelar su nombre porque sus términos de uso “incluyen no divulgar información confidencial”. “Muchas veces te dan un tema y tienes que escribir un prompt relacionado. El modelo de IA sacará dos respuestas, y al menos una debe tener un error. A continuación, evalúas cada respuesta de acuerdo a los criterios que fija el proyecto: si sigue las instrucciones, si la información es correcta, si el registro es apropiado, si el formato del texto es bueno, y después comparas ambas respuestas, eligiendo una ganadora”, añade este matemático español. El nuevo informe pretende sacar a la luz prácticas más dudosas sobre Outlier, que pueden tener un impacto en la legislación de la Unión Europea: “Lo que no siempre saben [los colaboradores europeos de Outlier] es cuántos datos personales recopilan sobre ellos estas empresas a través de la plataforma al ofrecer su trabajo como servicio”, dice Thomas Le Bonniec, autor principal del estudio e investigador en Sociología en el Instituto Politécnico de París. Le Bonniec ha hablado con 35 colaboradores europeos de Outlier en 12 países, quienes han compartido el tráfico de red de su computadora para investigar el acceso de la plataforma a sus equipos. El informe es obra del DiPLab, grupo de investigación académica, codirigido por el sociólogo Antonio Casilli en París, que estudia el trabajo humano invisible detrás de la IA, y Reversing.Works, un equipo técnico que aplica ingeniería inversa a aplicaciones de la “economía de plataformas” [o gig economy] para documentar prácticas opacas. ScaleAI, a través de Meta, no ha respondido a las preguntas de este periódico. Cada movimiento del ratón queda registrado La plataforma no solo obtiene conocimiento para entrenar modelos de IA, sino también datos personales sin que los trabajadores lo sepan, dice el informe. En sus navegadores hay rastreo de terceros, recogida biométrica a través de la app Persona y la monitorización de su actividad laboral incluye pulsaciones del teclado, movimientos del ratón y capturas de pantalla, sobre todo con el software FullStory. “El sistema registra cada vez que el ratón pasa por encima de un elemento de una página web o hace clic en él”, dice Simone Robutti, informático de la organización Reversing-Works. “A partir de esa información se reconstruye después el movimiento, con un nivel de detalle comparable al de una grabación de pantalla. Outlier no puede usar este sistema para rastrear a los usuarios fuera de su dominio. Pero FullStory, como empresa externa, podría en teoría identificar al mismo usuario en distintos dominios y cruzar las acciones realizadas en Outlier con las realizadas en otra web que también use FullStory, pero por ahora no tenemos forma de demostrarlo”, añade. Los trabajadores apenas saben nada de estos detalles. Los autores del informe se reunieron con una colaboradora anónima que había participado en el informe: “Ya sabía que me estaba metiendo en unas condiciones de trabajo o de protección de datos que probablemente no eran las mejores. Pero leer el informe fue muchísimo peor de lo que esperaba”, dijo. El matemático español no tuvo siquiera esas sospechas iniciales: “Al registrarme y aplicar a un área en particular (matemáticas, programación), tuve que subir mi currículum y dar mi perfil de LinkedIn, además de responder alguna pregunta. También fue necesario verificar mi identidad, o bien con mi DNI o con mi cara a través de una aplicación de autenticación, que no era sospechosa. Más allá de esto, no recuerdo haber cedido ningún permiso para recabar datos extra”, explica el matemático español. Esa app de terceros, Persona, tiene su sede en San Francisco: “Me han pedido identificarme con Persona unas siete u ocho veces en dos años. Sobre todo escaneando la cara, de frente y de los dos lados. Nunca me explicaron cómo se usaban esos datos”, dijo la trabajadora. La gestión de los ingresos es también delicada. Según la trabajadora que participó en el encuentro, Outlier paga por Paypal. No está claro cómo se resuelven los impuestos, más allá de una oscura empresa filipina mencionada en charlas informales entre trabajadores. Los autores del informe creen que Outlier incumple la regulación europea tal como está hoy. Creen que la desregulación que impulsa la Comisión podría debilitar artículos del RGPD que funcionan hoy como cortafuegos que frenan la transferencia de datos y conocimiento hacia Estados Unidos. data.ai_summary: NVIDIA launched Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, a 120B open multimodal model for enterprise agents, on Oct. 15, 2026. The model scores 80.8% on CharXiv and 84% on Python code interpretation, and NVIDIA claims up to 5x higher throughput for agentic tasks. It is available via NIM and Dynamo deployment paths.
data.author: Ted Hisokawa

industries.name: Agents & Autonomous Workflows (Tool Use, Planning, Multi-Agent)
Enterprise Foundation Model Integration & APIs (Connectors, Governance, Deployment)

data.full_text:
News
NVIDIA launches Nemotron 3.5 Super VL for multimodal agents
NVIDIA introduced Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, a 120B open multimodal model aimed at specialized enterprise agents and workflow automation.
NVIDIA on Oct. 15, 2026, introduced Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, an open, customizable multimodal model designed for specialized enterprise agents that must read documents, inspect images and video, use tools and follow policy across longer workflows.
Evidence and context
According to NVIDIA’s technical blog published the same day, the model uses a 120 billion-parameter mixture-of-experts architecture with 12 billion active parameters per token. NVIDIA said the design is intended to balance model capacity with inference efficiency, and reported that on a single GPU the model delivers up to 5x higher throughput for agentic tasks than other open models in its size category.
The company said Nemotron 3.5 Super VL combines reasoning, instruction following and tool use with text, image, document and video understanding, allowing teams to handle multimodal tasks in one workflow rather than chaining separate text and vision models. NVIDIA also said developers can post-train the model with NeMo using proprietary data, tools, policies and workflows.
NVIDIA cited several customer-style deployments to illustrate the model’s intended use cases. Scale AI post-trained it for automated vendor credit processing at Skydance Corporation, which NVIDIA said will reduce inference cost for that workload by 40x and latency by 5x. Ramp is using it to convert receipt images into structured JSON, with NVIDIA saying Ramp expects up to 50% higher throughput and 10x lower latency. AI21 post-trained the model for Alice’s threat intelligence and vulnerability analysis, which NVIDIA said improved accuracy by 40%.
The company said the release includes base, post-trained and NVFP4-quantized checkpoints, along with training recipes, data and reinforcement-learning environments. NVIDIA also said it is releasing open datasets on Hugging Face covering agentic tool use, finance reasoning and tool-calling, instruction-following, long-context transduction, fairness and 45 vision-language datasets.
On benchmark comparisons provided by NVIDIA, Nemotron 3.5 Super VL scored 80.8% on CharXiv, versus 63% for Nemotron 3 Nano Omni, and 84% with Python code interpretation. NVIDIA also said the model scored higher than Nemotron 3 Ultra on Hermes Bench and LangChain behavioral evaluations, citing scores of 63.44% versus 56.33% on Hermes Bench and 87.05% versus 84.3% on LangChain.
For inference, NVIDIA highlighted LiLiCorr speculative decoding, NVFP4 quantization, multi-token prediction and context reuse across agent turns. The company said LiLiCorr can deliver up to 2.3x faster token generation than decoding without speculation on DGX Spark, and that NVIDIA Dynamo can serve up to 8x as many users while reducing first-token latency by 85% in a specific configuration on 16 NVIDIA B200 GPUs. Those figures were reported by NVIDIA and are configuration-specific rather than general guarantees.
The blog also said the model was distilled from Nemotron 3 Ultra and further trained with specialized text and vision teachers, with additional continued pretraining using Indic-language data. NVIDIA said it is releasing a dataset of about 2.8 trillion tokens across 22 Indian languages, developed with IIT Madras and its AI4Bharat lab.
OpenHands also published related material on Oct. 15, 2026, describing Nemotron 3.5 Super VL in visual agent workflows, while Multiverse Computing separately announced a multimodal model collaboration with NVIDIA the same day. NVIDIA’s post itself said the model is available through supported local, data center and cloud environments, including NIM and Dynamo deployment paths.

data.title: NVIDIA Releases Open Nemotron 3.5 Super VL and Bolt Edge Models
data.ai_summary: NVIDIA released Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, a 120-billion-parameter multimodal model, and two Bolt models for edge and local hardware. Super VL scores 63.44% on Hermes Bench and 87.05% on LangChain evaluations, with Bolt 74B-A9B available now and Bolt E4B 4GB on October 23, 2026.
data.author: Jonas Reeve
data.full_text:
NVIDIA released Nemotron 3.5 Super VL on October 15, 2026, an open 120-billion-parameter multimodal model aimed at specialized always-on agents, alongside two smaller Bolt models for edge and local hardware. Super VL and Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB are available now, with Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB scheduled for October 23, 2026. The releases expand a Nemotron family that NVIDIA organizes by deployment tier. Lightning, released in August, handles high-throughput workloads; Ultra takes the hardest reasoning tasks; and Bolt targets the edge. NVIDIA said the three new open models together cover the full range of agent deployments, from large enterprise servers down to edge devices and local hardware, and that Super VL was built in collaboration with the Nemotron Coalition. Architecture and Reported Performance Super VL uses a 120-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts architecture that activates 12 billion parameters per token. NVIDIA said the model delivers accuracy on multimodal agentic tasks, including instruction following, tool use, multistep business workflows, and visual understanding, comparable with its largest reasoning model at roughly one-fifth the parameter count. NVIDIA also describes it as the fastest open agentic model in its class, reporting up to 5x higher throughput than other open models in its size category on a single GPU. The model combines reasoning, instruction following, and tool use with text, image, document, and video understanding in a single system. According to NVIDIA’s technical blog, that integration lets teams handle text and visual tasks without deploying separate text and vision-language models or passing task context between them. NVIDIA said the model’s vision-language training targets what agents encounter in practice: optical character recognition, tables, charts, and structured information in visual documents such as web pages and PDFs. NVIDIA’s reported evaluations show Super VL scoring 63.44% on Hermes Bench and 87.05% on LangChain behavioral evaluations, against 56.33% and 84.3% for Nemotron 3 Ultra. On CharXiv, a chart-reasoning benchmark, NVIDIA reports 80.8% for Super VL versus 63% for Nemotron 3 Nano Omni, rising to 84% when the model uses Python code interpretation. NVIDIA also describes Super VL as one of the top open models on the OCRBench v2 leaderboard, and the technical blog states that an independent evaluation by EXO Labs placed it on the Pareto frontier for accuracy and task completion time on DGX Spark. Training and Inference Design Super VL was distilled from Nemotron 3 Ultra, with the technical blog crediting Ultra’s coding capabilities and the SkewReverse loss used during distillation for improved coding accuracy. During post-training, multi-teacher on-policy distillation combines guidance from specialized teachers across text and vision, with the teachers scoring the model’s responses for video reasoning and tracking, vision tool use, and alignment. The technical blog also notes contributions from Nemotron Coalition organizations: datasets from Perplexity supported the model’s mid-training, and environments from Prime Intellect were used to build teacher models. Nemotron 3.5 Super VL was trained on about 26 trillion tokens across pretraining and continued pretraining, then post-trained with roughly 3.8 million samples and reinforcement learning across dozens of environments. Continued pretraining added 10 billion Indic tokens, and NVIDIA is releasing a dataset of about 2.8 trillion tokens across 22 Indian languages developed with IIT Madras and its AI4Bharat lab. The release includes base, post-trained, and NVFP4-quantized checkpoints. The NVFP4 recipe uses 4-bit weights and activations on NVIDIA’s Blackwell architecture, paired with quantization-aware distillation intended to close the accuracy gap that quantization introduces. An open speculative decoding technique called LiLiCorr delivers up to 2.3x faster token generation than decoding without speculation on DGX Spark, NVIDIA reports. Multi-token prediction gives the model an internal drafter that proposes several tokens for verification in one forward pass, and context-reuse serving optimizations preserve both attention caches and Mamba recurrent states across repeated agent calls. Bolt Models at the Edge Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB uses native 2-bit quantization to fit in 24GB of memory and run locally on NVIDIA RTX and DGX Spark alongside other applications. NVIDIA describes it as the top open model in its class on PinchBench and the second-ranked open model on BrowseComp. The model is available on Hugging Face with support for llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio, Unsloth, and vLLM. It is built for NVIDIA RTX Spark laptops arriving October 16, 2026, and also runs on GeForce RTX PCs, DGX Spark, DGX Station, and RTX PRO workstations. Bolt E4B 4GB targets physical and conversational agents on GeForce RTX, Jetson, and RTX/DGX Spark, combining natural conversation with multi-turn agentic capabilities for local voice assistants, interactive characters, and embedded interfaces. Customization, Early Adopters, and Deployment The model ships with open weights, open datasets, and training recipes, with customization supported through NVIDIA NeMo, Python-based pipelines, and open datasets. NVIDIA is releasing open datasets on Hugging Face spanning agentic tool use, finance, instruction following, long context, fairness, and 45 vision-language datasets, along with reinforcement-learning environments in NeMo Gym. Dozens of organizations are post-training Super VL on their own data, tools, policies, and workflows, according to NVIDIA. Scale AI post-trained the model for Skydance’s vendor credit finance agent and EY’s M&A due diligence agent; the technical blog states that inference cost for the Skydance workload will decrease by 40x and latency by 5x. AfterQuery customized the model for Hebbia for credit agreement analysis, and AI21 and Alice post-trained it for cybersecurity attack resilience, with NVIDIA reporting 40% higher accuracy for Alice’s threat intelligence and vulnerability analysis. Mercor post-trained the model on the APEX-SWE coding benchmark for coding agents that plan, write, and debug code. Ramp is converting receipt images into structured JSON containing merchant information, dates, and payment data, and expects up to 50% higher throughput and 10x lower latency, according to the technical blog. Software platform companies integrating Super VL include Atlassian for agentic search across apps such as Jira and Confluence, CrowdStrike for agentic blue teaming in enterprise security, Dassault Systèmes for engineering design and simulation, and Perplexity for search and agentic tasks. Salesforce is customizing Nemotron to power AI agents that digitize and automate government workflows through Missionforce Operations, and Synopsys software for semiconductor design verification interoperates with the model. For deployment, NVIDIA NIM packages the model as a production-ready microservice refreshed every two weeks with security patches and performance improvements. NVIDIA reports that on 16 B200 GPUs at 50 tokens per second per user, Dynamo serving with KV-cache-aware routing serves up to 8x as many users while reducing first-token latency by 85%. Super VL is available now on Hugging Face, OpenRouter, ModelScope, and as NVIDIA NIM, running across DGX Spark, DGX Station, RTX PRO and RTX systems, Jetson, and data center and cloud environments.

data.title: Who Is Building Ground Truth for AI Agents? Top 5 best companies
data.ai_summary: Five companies—Scale AI, Keymakr, Surge AI, Labelbox, and Appen—are profiled as providers of ground truth data for AI agents. Each offers specialized platforms for labeling, RLHF, and evaluation, with Scale AI and Appen noted for large-scale projects. The article emphasizes that ground truth quality determines agent performance.
data.author: Balla

industries.name: RLHF, Human Feedback & Evaluation Data Tools
Data Quality, Validation & Ground Truth Auditing

data.full_text:
As AI agents become increasingly complex, the importance of the high-quality data they are trained on grows as well. Modern agentic systems require high-precision ground truth datasets, human feedback, response evaluation, chains of thought, and data for RLHF. This is exactly why companies engaged in data preparation and validation have become key elements of the AI ecosystem. What to look for when choosing a data provider? Before choosing a ground truth provider for AI agents, several factors should be evaluated: Quality control and verification – a reliable QA technology that combines automated algorithmic checks with multi-level human auditing.

Availability of subject matter experts – complex AI systems can only be created by people with relevant expertise.

Support for RLHF and model evaluation – modern models heavily rely on human feedback and evaluation.

Tools and integration – the ability to process large volumes of data and work with multiple languages and data types.

Security and compliance – strict adherence to GDPR, ISO/IEC 27001, and SOC 2 standards, especially if agents will work with confidential corporate data.

A combination of human expertise and automation allows maintaining both quality and speed simultaneously. Top 5 companies building ground truth for AI agents 1. Scale AI One of the most prominent giants of the industry and a key partner for leading AI laboratories (OpenAI, Meta, Microsoft). The company has built a massive ecosystem for generative AI, LLMs, autonomous systems, and next-generation agents. In addition to classic labeling, they specialize in RLHF, model testing, performance evaluation, and AI safety. Thanks to its colossal infrastructure, the company can support large-scale, ultra-complex projects. The company has its own Scale GenAI platform and a network of subject-matter experts who provide reinforcement learning and model evaluation services at an industrial scale. Best suited for: large AI companies that need millions of volumes of high-quality textual and multimodal data within tight deadlines. 2. Keymakr The company has made a powerful leap forward by offering targeted solutions specifically for agentic AI, computer vision, NLP, and complex autonomous systems. Instead of scattering efforts across standard mass labeling, they combine high-precision manual annotation from their in-house team with automated quality-control tools. A flexible approach and the ability to work with custom requirements make the company attractive to both startups and enterprise clients. Their own Keylabs platform is a powerful proprietary enterprise solution for image, video, and 3D data annotation with integrated ML automation algorithms, annotator action tracking, and multi-level QA management. They involve subject matter experts to write complex chains of thought and deploy them in RLHF. Best suited for: custom AI projects, computer vision, multimodal agents, developers of deep research systems, and robotics. 3. Surge AI A company that shifted the focus from quantity to the flawless quality of human feedback. It focuses on creating datasets for complex tasks related to logical reasoning, security, and model alignment. Thanks to this, Surge AI has become one of the key players in the field of data preparation for modern LLMs and AI agents that must operate with nuances of language and context. The platform utilizes a unique framework for adversarial testing, allowing humans to intentionally “break” models to identify vulnerabilities, alongside automated LLM-based QC bots to verify human labeling. Best suited for: RLHF tasks, building reasoning datasets, alignment tasks, and deep model evaluation. 4. Labelbox This provider offers complex software to the market. Labelbox positions itself as a full-fledged data management platform, providing clients with tools for dataset preparation, process automation, model evaluation, and the organization of human feedback within a single interface. The Labelbox platform includes modules for data management, labeling, and testing & evaluation. It allows companies to centralize their data operations. Instead of simply buying a ready-made dataset, teams get an environment where they can automate labeling with their own models and flexibly integrate both internal annotators and external crowdsourced workers. Best suited for: teams and companies seeking full control and tools to manage the entire data lifecycle and build their own AI infrastructure. 5. Appen One of the oldest, largest, and most experienced players in the global AI data market. The company’s main advantage is a colossal global network of contributors and support for hundreds of languages and dialects, allowing it to collect and annotate large-scale multilingual text, audio, and visual datasets. The Appen platform automates task distribution and quality control across a network of millions of contributors. It offers the capability to scale rapidly in geography and language. For AI agent developers, this means access to ground truth data that accounts for local cultural contexts, speech specifics, and local regulatory requirements. Best suited for: large-scale data collection, AI localization, and large multilingual projects for international markets. Who holds the keys to the autonomous future? The irony of artificial intelligence development is that the more autonomous AI agents become, the more heavily they depend on humans during their formative stage. We attempt to delegate complex work to machines – from managing investment portfolios to performing surgical operations – but the safety of this transition rests entirely on the shoulders of ground truth providers. The companies we reviewed today are literally writing the rules of the game by which the global digital economy will live tomorrow. When building your own AI agent, it is essential to consider that while the model architecture or algorithms represent the car’s chassis, the ground truth is its fuel, engine, and roadmap. And the cleanliness and expertise of this fuel will determine whether your agent reaches its destination or spins out on the very first sharp turn of the real world. Author: Balla

data.title: AI companies are paying workers worldwide to record their jobs so robots can learn to do them
data.ai_summary: AI companies are paying workers worldwide to record physical tasks for robot training, with demand for such data up 10 times in a year. Robotics companies raised $33.4 billion in the first half of 2025, and the AI training dataset market is projected to grow from $11.9 billion to $49.8 billion by 2031.
data.author: Rya Jetha
data.full_text:
One Friday evening this summer, a private chef prepared a three-course meal — burrata salad, baked salmon, and tiramisu — for two friends and me.
The dinner was free, but there was a catch. A camera mounted on Chef Aliser Demir's baseball cap was recording everything.
Demir came to my apartment through Shift, the data-collection arm of the German startup Microagi. The startup offers free private chefs in San Francisco in exchange for first-person footage of their work. Shift offered to pay Demir, who runs a private chef business, his usual rate of $100 to $150 per person.
"I've been feeding people since I started this job," Demir said. "Now I am also feeding AI."
Demir is part of a global effort to collect data on how humans interact with the physical world, with the goal of building machines that can staff factories, clean homes, and even fight wars. Elon Musk, who is betting Tesla's future on the humanoid robot Optimus, has promoted a utopian future of "sustainable abundance," in which AI and robots make human labor largely optional.
For now, those ambitions face a problem: a massive shortage of training data. "It is widely agreed in the robotics world that data is the key bottleneck," said Kyle Chan, a fellow at the Brookings Institution who studies technology and industrial policy.
This is the third installment of the AI Data Grab, Business Insider's series on how human work is becoming raw material for AI — and the companies that are cashing in. So far, we've reported on how AI labs are buying up employees' emails and Slack messages, and how law firms are turning decades of human expertise into AI systems. Now, the scramble is moving into the physical world, where companies are paying people to record skills robots have yet to learn.
Contract workers in Mexico and the Philippines remotely control robots in American warehouses as they pack beauty products, recording movements so the machines can eventually do the work on their own. Other workers across the world strap cameras to their foreheads to capture first-person footage of themselves folding laundry and making hotel beds.
"This is how the great knowledge transfer happens from humans to robots," said Josh Gruenstein, CEO of Tutor Intelligence. His company operates a Massachusetts "data factory" where workers remotely control robots to generate training data.
A booming data market
Demand for robot training data is roughly 10 times higher than a year ago, Vineeth Velmurugan, who leads robot learning at the AI data startup Encord, said. Encord's customers, including Dyna Robotics and Agility Robotics, once requested 1,000 hours of annotated data. Now they want 10,000 or even 100,000, he said.
That red-hot demand for real-world data comes as robotics has become one of Silicon Valley's hottest bets. Humanoid robot makers Figure AI and Agility Robotics have fetched multibillion-dollar valuations, as have the companies developing robot "brains" such as Skild AI and Physical Intelligence.
Robotics companies raised $33.4 billion globally in the first half of this year, according to PitchBook data, surpassing the $28.7 billion raised in all of 2025. Cheaper hardware and computing, better AI models, labor shortages, and competition with China are all fueling investor interest.
But a gulf remains between robots that perform impressive demos and machines reliable enough to work an eight-hour factory shift. Robotics companies hope more training data will help, and suppliers across the world, from scrappy startups to established companies like Scale AI, Instawork, and Uber, are rushing to sell it to them.
Custom hardware is key to recording the physical world. Mecka AI, which has raised more than $120 million from investors including Sequoia and Nvidia, started with an app that paid people to record everyday activities two years ago. But the company soon ran into the limits of ordinary video.
Mecka now designs headgear and sensor-equipped gloves to "sensorize humans," CEO Josh Gao said. The equipment records movements and force, such as the pressure needed to grip a glass or crack an egg. Contractors label workplace footage before Mecka sells it to AI labs and robotics companies.
Microagi, the parent company of Shift, is expanding its collection efforts into homes and workplaces across more than 15 countries. It pays more than 35,000 people to record themselves performing physical tasks, CEO Bercan Kilic said. Shift said participants can earn up to $30 an hour and that it has paid out around $10 million in 2026.
Household chores are the most common, but unusual tasks help expose models to unfamiliar situations. One contributor in Turkey records himself repairing old jet engines in his garage, Kilic said.
Kilic's goal is to gather enough data to build robots that can work in factories and address labor shortages in Europe and the US. "If you run factories, the math is already on your desk," Kilic previously told Business Insider. "Your most experienced people retire this decade, and their replacements were never born. Reshoring only works if the robots do."
Income today, automation tomorrow
For the workers supplying that data, though, the trade-off is income today in exchange for helping build machines that could eventually automate their work.
Demir, the private chef, said he believes his work is safe. "Machines can just watch, listen, and follow instructions," he said. "They cannot feel or smell."
The economics are different in countries where labor is cheaper. Human Archive, a data collection company based in San Francisco, began building operations in India last year through partnerships with gig platforms, hotels, and plumbing and electrical businesses. It started with an app that let people record audio and first-person video. The startup now also makes custom hardware in China, including camera-equipped headsets and wrist trackers that capture movement.
Today, it operates in more than 30 countries and pays workers between $1 to $10 and "even much more," per hour, depending on how disruptive the equipment is, CEO Raj Patel said. These workers, Patel said, could earn "almost as much, or more [than their regular jobs], to just wear these devices."
Mecka and Human Archive did not say how they ensure workers' consent when collecting data through partner businesses or local contractors. Shift said participation is voluntary, and some employees at partner businesses choose not to participate. The company said it obtains explicit consent, explaining what data is collected and how it is used, including that it may be licensed to other labs for AI and robotics training.
The global competition for data work can come with a downside. It drives down wages and leaves workers with little bargaining power, said Mark Graham, a professor at the Oxford Internet Institute and author of Feeding the Machine, a book about the labor behind AI. "Often the workers don't even know what they're doing," he said. "They're a very disposable appendage of a much bigger machine."
The work can also be physically taxing. One operator who remotely controls robots in US warehouses from a Texas facility previously told Business Insider that eight-hour shifts cause arm and shoulder cramps. "We even have a massage gun in the office," they said.
Will the data boom last?
The companies collecting all this data are betting that the quest to train intelligent robots will fuel demand for years to come. Research firm Mordor Intelligence projects that the broader AI training dataset market will grow from $11.9 billion this year to nearly $49.8 billion by 2031.
For robotics data suppliers, the bull case is that startups will spend a significant share of their funding on training material, said Siddharth Ramakrishnan, a partner at Scale Venture Partners.
"If scaling laws continue to work, the pie will just keep growing," he said.
But nobody knows how much data robots will need to work reliably, he added. If they need less than expected, data suppliers could lose business. If they need much more, investors could tire of paying before the robots become commercially viable.
Some are betting that demand for robot training data is nowhere near its peak. Encord's Velmurugan likens today's robot brain to that of a two-year-old, and estimates that training a robot to work in homes — one of the hardest environments because it is so unstructured — could require a dataset five times the size of YouTube. At the end of 2025, YouTube held an estimated 29 billion videos, the equivalent of 280,000 years of footage, according to research firm Omdia.
"It's hard to say how this will play out," Ken Goldberg, a UC Berkeley robotics professor and cofounder of warehouse robotics startup Ambi Robotics, said. "It might take five years or 50 years. And even if we had unlimited data now, I don't know if this approach will work," he said.
Training robots in virtual environments, known as simulation, could also change the equation. World Labs, a startup slated for an $8.2 billion acquisition by AMD, says it can turn a small set of recordings into simulated environments and modify them to generate more training data for robots. If the technology delivers, robotics companies could need far less data from the physical world.
But even sustained demand doesn't guarantee a profitable business.
Earlier this year, Sam Padilla shut down his robotics data startup, Eidon AI, after struggling with logistics, upfront costs, and thin margins. He compared the business to dropshipping, where retailers sell goods shipped directly by suppliers and pocket the markup — until competitors offering the same products for less squeeze their margins.
"There is a clear arbitrage opportunity to make money if you're willing to race and race to the bottom," he said. "But a technical bottleneck does not necessarily imply a good business."

data.title: SWE-bench
data.ai_summary: SWE-bench is a benchmark for language models on software engineering tasks, with 2,294 tasks from 12 Python repositories. OpenAI's SWE-bench Verified, a human-validated subset, saw a leading result of 80.9% in February 2026, but OpenAI said it would stop quoting the figure due to contamination. The company recommended switching to SWE-bench Pro.
data.full_text:
Benchmark for language models on software engineering tasks SWE-bench is a benchmark for large language models and coding agents. Its 2,294 tasks were taken from issues that were actually filed, and actually fixed, in 12 Python repositories: astropy, django, flask, matplotlib, pylint, pytest, requests, scikit-learn, seaborn, sphinx, sympy and xarray. Django alone supplies 850 of them, sympy another 386. The system being tested is shown the repository as it stood before the fix, plus the text of the issue, and has to produce a patch. It never sees the tests that will judge the result. When the benchmark was introduced in October 2023 by a group at Princeton University and the University of Chicago, under the title "Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?", the strongest model they tried, Claude 2, fixed only 1.96% of the tasks.[1] In August 2024, OpenAI released SWE-bench Verified, a human-validated subset of SWE-bench. In February 2026, the leading published result on SWE-bench Verified was 80.9%. In a post titled "Why SWE-bench Verified no longer measures frontier coding capabilities", OpenAI said it would stop quoting the figure at all. The models being scored had read the repositories the tasks come from, and in the sample OpenAI examined every frontier model it tried could reproduce wording from the problem statements or from the developers' own fix. OpenAI recommended switching to SWE-bench Pro, another variant.[2]

Variants [ edit ] SWE-bench Verified, put together with OpenAI in August 2024, is the version model releases usually quote: 500 tasks whose descriptions and tests were read through by human annotators first.[3][2] Three spin-offs followed: Lite (300 tasks that each touch a single file, cheaper to run), Multimodal (617 tasks from JavaScript interface libraries, each with an image in the issue or the tests) and Multilingual (300 tasks in nine languages).[4][5][6] Scale AI's SWE-Bench Pro, from September 2025, answers the contamination problem by keeping much of itself secret: of its 1,865 tasks, one part is withheld and another comes from private repositories.[7] A 2026 paper found the same leakage there and published a corrected version.[8]

data.title: Muse Wonder来了，扎克伯格复仇成功了吗？
data.ai_summary: Meta released Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full on October 12, with the Full version outperforming OpenAI and Anthropic flagship models in benchmarks. The models support 1 million-token context and feature active memory and focus, but face pricing and API access challenges. Meta's next Agent competition depends on user trust and ecosystem integration.

industries.name: Enterprise Foundation Model Integration & APIs (Connectors, Governance, Deployment)

data.full_text:
扎克伯格终于等来了自己的翻身仗。 当地时间10月12日，Meta发布新一代大模型Muse Wonder和Muse Wonder Full。根据官方公布的Benchmark，性能更强的Wonder Full在多项Agent和编程测试中超越OpenAI、Anthropic的旗舰模型，第三方评测也显示，Meta已经重新跻身前沿模型第 一梯队。 但就在一年半前，情况还完全不同。 外部，OpenAI、Anthropic的双强格局仿佛尘埃落定，Meta一度被认为在前沿模型竞争中掉队。内部，扎克伯格押上千亿美元级别的AI基础设施投资，花上亿美元高薪“雇佣兵”式狂挖研究员，种种决策没少遭到挖苦。 如今，Meta终于拿出了阶段性成果。 扎克伯格复仇成功了吗？模型能力追上了OpenAI和Anthropic，Meta能赢得下一场Agent战争吗？ 我们整理了昨天扎克伯格和Meta首席AI官汪滔采访中的核心观点以供阅读： 模型正在成为产品本身。 Meta内部常说“The model is the product”。Agent的差异不再只是界面，而是记忆、主动性、可靠性和交互体验。这些能力需要通过训练数据、后训练和评测塑造，产品设计正逐渐深入模型层。 过度追求跑分，等于把产品方向交给别人。 汪滔认为，如果一味围绕外部Benchmark优化，就相当于把产品决策交给制定评测的人。Meta早期追赶时重视外部排名，如今更关注针对真实用户场景设计的内部评测。 模型进步不一定依赖重新预训练。 Muse Spark从1.0到1.3沿用同一基座模型，主要通过强化学习提升能力。Meta同时推进两条路线：扩大预训练规模（逐级放大约4—5倍），以及优化强化学习方法。 Personal Agent需要更强的多模态能力。 汪滔认为，行业过度聚焦Coding，但普通用户更多通过视觉、语音和视频与世界交互。因此，Meta从预训练阶段就强化多模态能力，而非仅在后训练中补齐。 实验室的关键是人才密度和人均算力。 Meta采用小规模精英团队，集中分配算力，减少资源分散。扎克伯格强调扁平化管理，避免管理层脱离技术一线。 实验室负责人的战略判断比履历更重要。 尽管汪滔此前没有直接领导前沿模型训练的经验，扎克伯格仍看重他的战略思考、快速调整能力，以及吸引顶 尖研究人员的能力。 01 经典跑分环节 先给出判断，这次的新模型是能长期记住用户使用习惯、跨软件完成任务的Personal Agent底座模型。 Muse Wonder和性能更强的Muse Wonder Full，都支持100万Token上下文窗口，能够理解文本、图像、音频和视频，原生输出以文本为主。相比上一代Muse Spark系列，新模型重点强化了编程、长期Agent任务和专业知识工作。Meta确认，Muse Wonder未来将成为个人Agent Muse的核心模型。 其中，最值得关注的是两项能力。 一是Active Memory（主动记忆），让Agent能够跨对话记住用户偏好，在需要时主动提取相关信息，而不必反复询问。二是Active Focus（主动聚焦），让Agent在执行复杂任务时持续尝试、纠错，遇到障碍能够调整方案，而不是直接放弃。 Meta还展示了根据图片制作可交互3D游戏、跨应用规划跑步活动、自动生成婚礼座位表等案例。 那么，新模型究竟有多强？ 按照Meta公布的官方Benchmark，Wonder Full在多项Agent和编程测试中已经超过OpenAI、Anthropic的旗舰模型。 Meta专门设计了一项Personal Superintelligence Index（个人超级智能指数），综合衡量专业工作、流程自动化、网页操作等七类任务。 在这项测试中，Wonder Full取得59.1%的成绩，超过Claude Opus 5.5的55.2%和GPT-6 Astra的54.5%。 在考察端到端业务流程自动化能力的AutomationBench-AA中，Wonder Full取得45.4%，同样高于Astra的41.6%和Opus 5.5的41.2%。 长期记忆也是Meta的优势项目。在内部开发的MemoryBench测试中，普通版Wonder和Wonder Full分别取得85.6%和85.5%，均高于Opus 5.5和Astra的约81%。 编程方面，Wonder Full在长期软件工程测试SWE-Marathon中取得57.5%的成功率，领 先Opus 5.5的46.3%和Astra的42.5%。 第三方机构Artificial Analysis（AA）的综合测评则给出了更客观的参照。 在Intelligence Index v4.3中，Wonder Full获得56分，普通版Wonder为52分，较上一代Muse Spark 1.3的48分分别提升8分和4分。作为对比，Claude Opus 5.5为58分，GPT-6 Astra为53分。 这意味着，Wonder Full已经进入前沿模型第 一梯队，但综合表现目前还没有全面超越竞争对手。 但漂亮的跑分，并没有换来一致的口碑。 Wonder发布后，部分开发者在X上质疑，Meta是否过度针对Benchmark优化模型，以至于实际体验与榜单排名存在落差。 争议最集中的是3D游戏生成任务。有开发者晒出测试结果，认为Wonder的表现明显不及其他前沿模型。 面对质疑，Meta首席AI官汪滔承认，团队此前并未专门针对3D演示游戏训练模型，希望开发者更多关注其真实软件工程能力。 但有用户直接回怼，视频游戏演示也是通过代码做出来的，“游戏怎么不算‘实际编程工作’？”，并且对其泛化能力产生怀疑。 最后，开放范围和价格也是槽点。 Muse Wonder API每百万Token输入4美元、输出20美元，缓存输入0.2美元，与Claude Opus 5.5的基础输入、输出定价持平，是Gemini 4 Argon的两倍。第三方测算显示，Wonder每项测试任务的成本约为4.52美元，高于GPT-6 Astra的3.26美元，也超过了Gemini。 而性能更强的Wonder Full暂未开放独立API，目前仅向Muse Code的Power Usage和Maximum Usage订阅用户提供，订阅价格分别为每月50美元和200美元。 以及值得注意的是，此次两款模型均未公开权重。曾经以Llama开放模型闻名的Meta，这一次选择了更加封闭的发布方式。 02 Meta的千亿美元翻身仗 过去一年多，围绕Meta大模型最多的声音，是质疑。 2025年4月，曾被寄予厚望的Llama 4发布后，因性能不及预期、Benchmark评测争议等问题遭到外界质疑。曾经凭借Llama系列领跑开放模型市场的Meta，逐渐在前沿模型竞争中掉队。 扎克伯格坐不住了。他在Llama 4于2025年4月4日发布仅仅两周后，就开始联系外部研究人员，寻求重建AI团队的建议。 这一次，他决定几乎推倒重来：调整原有研发路线，重新组建团队。 而他找到的关键人物之一，就是Scale AI联合创始人汪滔。 当时汪滔正在开员工会议，突然收到扎克伯格的一条WhatsApp消息，询问他是否有时间通话。两人随后聊了约44分钟。两天后，汪滔给扎克伯格发来一份长篇方案，具体解释了如果由自己掌管Meta的AI业务的话，会怎么做。 方案的第 一条就是：不要太多人，关键在于人才密度。 扎克伯格被说服了。 2025年6月，Meta将汪滔招至麾下，斥资约143亿美元获得数据标注公司Scale AI的49%股权，汪滔出任Meta首席AI官，并成立超级智能实验室（MSL）。 汪滔此前从来过领导前沿大模型训练的经验。但扎克伯格认为，汪滔就是那个Mr. Right。他能给Meta带来的，不只是一套技术方案，更是一种接近创业公司的组织方式。 接下来的故事我们都知道了，Meta开始从OpenAI、Google、xAI等竞争对手手中狂挖研究员，且金额巨大。 扎克伯格说，那一两个月时间内，他几乎清空自己的日程，密集会见研究员。那段时间他和汪滔都没有怎么睡觉。 根据路透社的报道，Meta曾向部分研究人员提出四年最高3亿美元、第 一年总薪酬超过1亿美元的offer。 这场人才争夺甚至出现了颇具硅谷特色的一幕，扎克伯格甚至曾亲自给想招募的研究员送汤。 扎克伯格希望用少数顶 尖人才组成一支精锐团队，再向他们集中分配算力资源。据披露，目前Meta负责核心模型研发的研究团队不足200人。 但这场组织重建并非一帆风顺，人员摩擦和变动一直在发生。金融时报报道显示，Meta在半年内经历四次AI领导层调整。曾参与ChatGPT研发的赵晟佳（Shengjia Zhao）加入后，一度考虑返回OpenAI，随后才被任命为Meta首席AI科学家。另外两名新招募的研究人员Ethan Knight、Avi Verma也在短暂加入Meta后返回OpenAI。 与此同时，扎克伯格还在投入巨额资金建设算力基础设施。 据路透社报道，Meta将2026年资本开支预期提高至1300亿到1450亿美元，主要用于AI基础设施等领域。与此同时，Meta正在建设俄亥俄州的Prometheus集群和路易斯安那州的Hyperion集群，规划规模分别超过1吉瓦和达到5吉瓦。 如此巨大的投入，Meta内部其实也在打鼓。 扎克伯格回忆，2025年底，他与汪滔讨论过一笔1000亿至2000亿美元量级的投资决定。当时模型结果尚不明朗，他还问过汪滔：“你确定这能成功吗？” 汪滔自己也说，在夏威夷举行的一次高管会议上，Meta首席财务官Susan Li曾多次把他拉到一旁，提醒他：如果模型失败，财务后果会非常严重。 如今，Muse Wonder终于发布。 虽然仍有争议。但对于这支重建一年多的团队来说，它至少证明，Meta还是能有训练前沿模型的能力。 只是，这场耗资惊人的豪赌，距离真正证明商业价值，还有很长一段路要走。 03 模型能帮Meta赢下比赛吗？ 扎克伯格已经明确了自己的押注方向——Agent和Agent的模型。 他提出一个观点：The model is the product（模型就是产品）。在他看来，传统软件的界面会越来越轻，决定产品体验的核心将是模型本身，包括记忆能力、可靠性、性格，以及调用工具完成任务的能力。这就是为什么Meta要从底层训练面向Personal Agent的模型。 但重新回到前沿模型第 一梯队，Meta就一定能赢得下一场Agent战争吗？ 目前来看，答案还远不确定。 用户留存首先是一个问题。华尔街日报报道显示，Muse已经获得近900万次全球下载，但相比ChatGPT等竞争对手，用户留存仍面临挑战。 其次是Agent的开放性问题。 Meta拥有Facebook、Instagram、WhatsApp等庞大的用户生态，并在AI眼镜等硬件入口上提前布局。相比独立Agent创业公司，Meta天然具备触达用户的优势。 但有入口，不等于能替用户办成事。今年9月，Muse上线不到两周，就遭到Amazon封禁。据彭博社报道，Amazon此前要求Meta停止让Muse操作其购物网站，遭到拒绝 后，直接阻止Muse访问平台。 这是Personal Agent的一道核心壁垒。即便Meta拥有数十亿用户，也无法保证其他互联网平台对Muse的开放。 其次是商业化的问题。 更强的模型也意味着更高的推理和服务成本。按照Meta目前的规划，Muse Wonder将优先接入每月20美元和100美元的Muse付费订阅服务。扎克伯格承认，Wonder体量更大，服务成本更高，因此暂时无法向所有免费用户全面开放。 所以，Meta不仅要让用户愿意尝试Muse，还要说服他们愿意长期使用、持续付费。这对于一个新产品来说，意味着推广难度上升。 当然，对于Meta这样一家广告业务庞大的互联网公司，Agent的商业价值也未必完全来自订阅收入。未来，它可能进一步融入社交、购物、广告和智能硬件生态，成为连接用户与商业服务的新入口。但这种商业模式能否成立，目前仍缺乏验证。 所以，下一阶段的Agent竞争，已经不再只是Benchmark上的分数之争。 能否赢得用户信任、打通外部生态，并以可控的成本稳定完成复杂任务，将成为决定Agent竞争格局的关键。 【本文由投资界合作伙伴虎嗅网授权发布，本平台仅提供信息存储服务。】

data.title: Alexandr Wang’s run at Meta Superintelligence Labs draws a fresh endorsement
data.ai_summary: Meta's X post endorsed Alexandr Wang as the right leader of Meta Superintelligence Labs, citing his strategic thinking and talent focus. Wang co-founded Scale AI, and Meta invested $14.3 billion for a 49% stake. MSL's Muse model launches and the Muse AI app's No. 1 App Store debut followed.
data.author: Diego Almada Lopez
data.full_text:
Alexandr Wang’s run at Meta Superintelligence Labs draws a fresh endorsement

A post on X credits the Scale AI co-founder's strategic thinking and talent focus as Meta's AI bet keeps paying out

by Diego Almada Lopez an hour ago

Alexandr Wang is getting another public vote of confidence. A post on X this week endorsed him as the right person to lead Meta Superintelligence Labs, singling out his strategic thinking and his obsession with talent. How Wang ended up running Meta’s AI ambitions Meta Superintelligence Labs, or MSL, launched on June 30, 2025. CEO Mark Zuckerberg unveiled it in an internal memo that reorganized the company’s AI efforts under one roof. Wang was named Chief AI Officer and head of MSL that same day. The appointment came alongside a deal that made it hard to miss. Meta invested $14.3 billion in Scale AI, the data company Wang co-founded. That money bought a 49% stake and valued Scale AI at approximately $29 billion. Wang stepped down as Scale AI’s CEO to take the job. He still sits on the company’s board. MSL includes several subgroups, among them TBD Lab, which focuses on frontier models. In July 2025, MSL named Shengjia Zhao as Chief Scientist. The results that make the praise stick In April 2026, MSL launched the Muse Spark model family, the first of its Muse models. AI, tech, and the markets they move—in one daily briefing. Daily. Free. Join 34,000+ readers across crypto, finance, and policy. We respect your privacy. Unsubscribe anytime. In September 2026, Meta rolled out the Muse AI app. It climbed to No. 1 in the Apple App Store. Meta’s stock rose by nearly 20% in the aftermath. Wang has framed MSL’s goal as building what he calls “personal superintelligence.” Who Wang is, and why Meta bet on him Born in 1997, Wang co-founded Scale AI in 2016, at age 19. The company started out in data labeling. By 2021, at age 24, Wang had become the world’s youngest self-made billionaire. The X endorsement leaned on two traits: strategic thinking and talent focus. Wang has prioritized what the research describes as talent density alongside aggressive investment. Talent density is the idea that a smaller team of exceptional people beats a larger team of good ones. What this means for Meta and the AI race For Meta shareholders, Wang’s tenure has turned a very expensive hire into something that looks more like a strategic win. The $14.3 billion Scale AI investment was a statement of intent. The Muse launches gave it a return that investors could actually see. The nearly 20% stock gain after the Muse app’s debut suggests the market is willing to reward Meta’s AI spending when that spending turns into products people download and use. Wang’s continued seat on Scale AI’s board is another detail to watch. Meta owns 49% of that company, so the relationship between the two will likely draw attention as both keep growing.

data.title: ‘MIT 중퇴’ 29세 청년…7개월만에 뮤즈 개발로 대성공
data.ai_summary: Meta's Wang CAIO, who left MIT at 19, joined Meta 7 months ago to develop Muze, an AI personal assistant. The app reached free app store top one in the US and Canada within two weeks of launch. Meta also released Muze Wonder and Muze Wonderful, with Muze Wonderful leading AI benchmarks.
data.author: 서울경제; 네이버
data.full_text:
스타트업 창업 후 메타에 합류
‘슈퍼인텔리전스 랩’서 뮤즈 개발
“해야할 일·하고픈 일 실현하는 AI”
“관료주의 반대”…200명과 대면
11일(현지 시간) 왕 CAIO는 팟캐스트 운영자 데이비드 센라와 인터뷰에서 메타 합류 7개월 만에 ‘뮤즈 돌풍’에 이르기까지 개발 과정을 전했다.
중국계 미국인인 왕 CAIO는 AI 학습용 데이터 라벨링 기업 ‘스케일AI’의 창업자다. 1997년생인 그는 매사추세츠공과대학교(MIT) 수학·컴퓨터과학과를 1학년 때 중퇴한 뒤 스케일AI를 설립했다. 그가 메타와 인연을 맺은 것은 메타가 지난해 AI 모델 ‘라마(Llama) 4’의 실패로 어려움에 처해있을 때다. 저커버그 CEO가 왕 CAIO에게 먼저 연락을 취한 지 5~6주 만에 메타는 스케일AI 지분 49%를 인수하는 형태로 왕 CAIO를 영입했다. MSL을 이끌게 된 그는 동시에 메타의 CAIO직을 맡게 됐다.
왕 CAIO는 당시 앤트로픽의 클로드 코드가 선두하는 ‘AI 코딩 에이전트’가 AI업계에 가장 중요한 화두였다고 회상했다. 가장 최적화된 AI 코딩 에이전트를 개발하는 AI 기업이 업계를 주도하게 될 것이라 예측됐다는 의미다. 그러나 왕 CAIO는 AI가 해야 하는 일을 처리해주는 ‘개인 초지능(personal superintelligence)’이란 개념에 집중했다.
왕 CAIO는 “마크(저커버그 CEO)에게 ‘우리가 인공일반지능(AGI)이나 인공초지능(ASI)을 이룬다면 메타는 정말 특별한 회사가 될 것’이라고 말했다”며 “우리의 삶은 ‘하고 싶은 일’과 ‘해야 할 일’로 나뉜다. AGI는 ‘해야 할 일’을 처리하는 한편, 메타의 기존 제품들은 ‘하고 싶은 일’도 돕는다”고 말했다. 메타가 AI로 사람의 일을 덜어주는 동시에 이를 통해 확보된 여가 시간을 보내는 서비스도 제공한다면 강력한 위치에 설 수 있다는 논리다.
왕 CAIO는 “메타 앱은 하루 35억 명의 사용자가 이용하는 만큼 메타의 성공은 소비자 AI에 달려 있다”며 “근본적으로 메타의 핵심은 개인”이라고 강조했다.
일반 소비자에 집중하는 메타의 전략은 성과를 보이고 있다. 지난달에 뮤즈 출시 2주 만에 미국과 캐나다 앱스토어에서 오픈AI의 챗GPT를 제치고 무료 앱 순위 1위에 오른 것이 대표적이다. 소비자들은 생활 밀착형 에이전트로 에이전트가 e메일을 대신 작성해 발송하거나 여행 관련 예약을 수행하고 온라인 쇼핑을 도와주는 편리함에 주목했다.
메타는 12일 최상위 AI 모델 시리즈인 뮤즈 원더와 고급형 ‘뮤즈 원더풀’도 출시했다. 메타는 원더를 유료 구독자에게 우선 제공해 수익화를 꾀할 계획이다. 미국 시장조사업체 아티피셜 애널리시스가 산출한 AI 종합 성능 지수에서는 뮤즈 원더풀이 오픈AI와 구글의 최신 모델을 앞섰다.
왕 CAIO는 메타가 중시하는 ‘관료제의 최소화’도 설명했다. 그는 “가장 똑똑하고 뛰어난 인재를 영입하는 것과 모든 구성원이 최고의 역량을 발휘할 수 있는 환경을 조성하는 것이 슈퍼인텔리전스 랩의 설립 이념”이라며 “메타에서 내 역할은 전통적인 ‘코치’에 가깝다”고 평가했다. 슈퍼인텔리전스 랩은 약 200명의 인원으로 구성돼 있지만 이들은 모두 왕 CAIO에게 직접 보고한다. 그 결과 이들은 올해 2월 메타 이사회에 AI 모델 기획 메모를 제출한 지 7개월 만에 뮤즈를 공개했다.

data.title: Zuckerberg says Meta made a $100 billion-plus AI infrastructure bet without knowing if it would work
data.ai_summary: Zuckerberg confirmed Meta committed $100–200 billion to AI infrastructure in late 2025 without successful models. CFO Susan Li raised concerns, but Meta proceeded, with 2026 capex at $130–145 billion. The company is building gigawatt-scale data centers and has secured nuclear power contracts.
data.author: Diego Almada Lopez

industries.name: AI Datacenter Power, Cooling & Racks (liquid cooling, power delivery)

data.full_text:
Meta Platforms logo (public domain) via Wikimedia Commons

Zuckerberg says Meta made a $100 billion-plus AI infrastructure bet without knowing if it would work

Meta's CEO says the company committed to a massive AI buildout in late 2025 before it had any successful models to show for it

by Diego Almada Lopez an hour ago

Mark Zuckerberg has confirmed something investors probably suspected. Meta committed an enormous sum to AI infrastructure without any guarantee the projects would pay off. According to Bloomberg, Zuckerberg said Meta spent hundreds of billions of dollars last year on AI infrastructure without knowing whether those projects would succeed. The bet, by the numbers The comments came in a podcast episode released on October 12–13, 2026. In it, Zuckerberg described a decision made in late 2025 to put between $100 billion and $200 billion into AI infrastructure. Meta made that commitment before it had developed any successful models. Chief financial officer Susan Li raised concerns about potential pitfalls of the plan, according to the research findings. Meta went ahead anyway. The company’s capital expenditure outlook for 2026 sits at $130–145 billion. That compares with $72 billion in 2025. Capital expenditure, or capex, is money a company spends on long-lived physical assets. For Meta, that means data centers, chips, and the power deals to keep them running. Meta’s infrastructure chief said more than $100 billion in 2026 alone is directed at infrastructure development. That includes custom silicon and energy sourcing. AI, tech, and the markets they move—in one daily briefing. Daily. Free. Join 34,000+ readers across crypto, finance, and policy. We respect your privacy. Unsubscribe anytime. During 2025, Meta lifted its capex estimates to a range of $64–72 billion as it pushed harder into AI. The 2026 range roughly doubles that, at least at the top end. What the money is building Meta is constructing gigawatt-scale data center clusters, including the Prometheus facility in Ohio and Hyperion in Louisiana. The company has secured nuclear power contracts totaling 6.5 GW through 2035. In 2025, Meta acquired a 49% stake in Scale AI for $14.3 billion to strengthen its AI efforts. Meta launched its new Muse Wonder models on October 12, 2026, the same window as the podcast. Meta claims the models match or exceed performance benchmarks against competing offerings from OpenAI and Anthropic. What this means for investors and the AI race The research findings note that the buildout has drawn scrutiny from investors and analysts focused on long-term returns, given the huge upfront costs. Zuckerberg’s candor confirms that the spending was a conviction call, not a response to proven demand from Meta’s own models. When a company’s top finance officer flags pitfalls and the CEO proceeds, the outcome tends to get attributed squarely to the CEO. Zuckerberg now owns this bet in a very public way. Data centers and power contracts are commitments that run for years, while AI model leadership can shift within months. Meta has locked in costs on a decade-long horizon to compete in a market that reshuffles constantly. What to watch next: independent evaluations of Muse Wonder, any revisions to the $130–145 billion capex range, and whether Meta can show revenue or engagement gains tied directly to its AI products.

data.title: Robotics labs are hunting for motion and video data to train AI models
data.ai_summary: Robotics labs are collecting motion and video data at scale to train AI models, with Dyna Robotics' Dyna-2 model seeing task success rise from 20% to 53% after expanding its dataset to over 1 million hours of egocentric footage. Innodata opened a motion-capture lab in New Jersey and Agile Robots announced a Robot Academy in Munich, while companies have raised nearly $48 billion in 2026 funding.
data.author: Diego Almada Lopez

industries.name: Simulation & Digital Twin Data for ML Training
AI & Machine Learning for Robotics Programs

data.full_text:
Robotics labs are hunting for motion and video data to train AI models

Developers are betting that first-person footage and precision motion capture can solve the data bottleneck holding back physical AI

by Diego Almada Lopez 27 minutes ago

Robots have a reading problem. Not literacy, exactly, but a shortage of the material they need to learn from. Robotics labs are now collecting motion and video data at scale to train the AI models that power their machines. The goal is simple to state and hard to pull off: teach robots to handle real-world tasks by showing them how humans do it. The push comes as the industry runs into what amounts to a data bottleneck. Building a robot that can fold laundry or sort parts requires examples of those tasks being performed. Lots of them. More footage, better robots The clearest evidence that this approach works comes from Dyna Robotics. Its Dyna-2 model saw task success climb from 20% to 53% in August 2026. The change behind that jump was the training dataset. Dyna expanded it from 1,000 hours to over 1 million hours of egocentric footage. Egocentric video is first-person footage, the kind captured from the viewpoint of whoever is doing the work. It shows the hands, the objects, and the sequence of movements from the angle a robot would actually experience. That result helps explain why massive human video pretraining has become a central pillar of robot development. It matters most for manipulation, meaning grabbing and handling objects, and for locomotion, meaning moving through physical space. AI, tech, and the markets they move—in one daily briefing. Daily. Free. Join 34,000+ readers across crypto, finance, and policy. We respect your privacy. Unsubscribe anytime. Building the data infrastructure Innodata opened a motion-capture research and development lab in Ridgefield Park, New Jersey, on September 30, 2026. The facility uses Vicon’s infrared optical cameras to track human and robot movements with sub-millimeter accuracy. Agile Robots announced its Robot Academy in Munich around October 8, 2026. The academy uses hand-tracking technology to turn ordinary videos of workers into usable trajectory data. That lets the company skip teleoperation rigs entirely. Companies like Scale AI are operating data factories and robot gyms across multiple countries, including Mexico, China, and Indonesia. Recording setups are distributed globally, and people perform tasks that get captured and fed into training pipelines. The money behind the movement Robotics and physical AI companies have raised nearly $48 billion in funding so far in 2026. That capital is landing during a notable shift in strategy. Developers are moving away from datasets generated mainly through simulation and toward large collections of human video and precision motion data. A generalist policy is a model that can handle many different tasks rather than one narrow job. It’s the difference between a factory arm that welds one seam forever and a machine that could plausibly be asked to do something new tomorrow. What this means for the robotics race The three approaches on display represent different tradeoffs. Innodata’s Vicon-equipped lab offers precision but limited throughput. Agile Robots’ worker-video method promises scale with less hardware. Distributed robot gyms trade some control for volume and geographic diversity. There are open questions worth watching. Distributing data collection across countries like Mexico, China, and Indonesia raises issues around labor conditions, consent, and how footage of workers is used. Turning ordinary job videos into training material, as Agile Robots plans, will likely invite similar scrutiny. Dyna went from 20% to 53% with a thousandfold data increase. A 53% success rate still means nearly half of attempts fail, which is not yet a number most factories or homes would accept.

data.title: Meta Stock Rallies Again As Wall Street Praises 'AI Reset'
data.ai_summary: Meta stock rallied on Tuesday after its Muse Wonder AI model drew bullish analyst attention. Truist raised its price target to 1,000 from 763, citing improved AI positioning. Meta reports third-quarter earnings on Oct. 21.
data.author: Ryan Deffenbaugh
data.full_text:
Meta Platforms (META) stock is rallying again on Tuesday, after the tech giant's latest Muse Wonder AI model brought bullish views from Wall Street.

Analysts with Truist upped their price target for Meta stock to 1,000 from 763 in a client note Tuesday morning. Truist analyst Youssef Squali said he expects the upcoming third-quarter results for Meta will add to the momentum for the stock that was sparked by Meta's Muse AI agent app.

"Meta's up 21% since Muse's launch on (Sept. 8) as the narrative around its AI positioning has improved materially," Squali wrote. "With AI infusing higher performance across ads, wearables and Muse — building non-ad revenues from powering personal superintelligence, Muse for Enterprise/(small- and medium-size businesses) — we see Meta as an AI winner long-term."

Squali reiterated a buy rating for Meta.

Meta's AI Reset

Meta's Muse Wonder large language model is a follow-up to its Muse Spark AI model. Chief Executive Mark Zuckerberg said called Wonder a state-of-the-art offering that puts Meta's AI lab at "the frontier."

Reaching the frontier lab status typically applied to Anthropic, OpenAI and Google parent Alphabet (GOOGL) has been a top goal of Zuckerberg's over the past 14 months. After Meta's models underwhelmed early last year, Zuckerberg initiated a drastic overhaul that saw the company spends billions to recruit top researchers.

That included a $14.3 billion investment in Scale AI that brought the start-up's founder Alexandr Wang on board as Meta's AI research leader.

The Wonder model will power Meta's Muse AI agent app for paying subscribers. It is also available in the Meta Model API and Muse Code offering for developers. In a blog post, Meta said the Wonder model outperforms Anthropic Claude Fable and OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra on some tasks.

Muse Wonder is evidence that Meta's "AI reset" is working, Squali wrote.

"Muse Wonder now puts Meta back at/near the top of the model rankings, per the referenced benchmark performances," Squali wrote. "On the monetization front, this is a paid consumer subscription plus a developer API, and it continues Meta's plan to build AI revenue outside advertising. Key to watch here will be adoption and retention at the $20/$100 price points against other gen-AI assistants, the cost of serving frontier models, and privacy, given the agent works across users' messages, calendars and documents."

Meta Stock: Earnings Due Next Week

Meta stock is up more than 3% at 766.59 on the stock market today. Shares climbed 3.4% on Monday.

The quick adoption of Meta's Muse AI assistant app helped power a 26.7% gain last month. But gains for Meta stock had eased over the first two weeks of October, prior to Monday's jump.

Shares have formed a massive 59-week consolidation pattern, as identified by IBD MarketSurge. Meta is chasing a record high 796.23 that shares reached in August 2025.

Meta will report third-quarter earnings on Oct. 21.
