data.full_text:
Meta Platforms Inc. (META) Stock: Gains $234 Billion in Five Days as AI Strategy Takes Off

Market Musing-g

TLDR

Meta stock climbs as AI strategy adds $234 billion in market value

New Muse AI agent reaches 2.8 million downloads across key markets

Meta unveils smart glasses and new AI-powered consumer devices

Alexandr Wang leads Meta’s expanding artificial intelligence strategy

Meta Connect highlights the company’s shift toward AI innovation

Meta Platforms Inc. (META) traded at $771.38, rising 3.67%, as the stock extended a strong five-day rally that added about $234 billion to its market value. The shares recovered from early weakness near the $720 support zone and moved above the $760 resistance level. The move followed renewed attention on Meta’s artificial intelligence strategy, new products, and hardware announcements.







Meta Platforms, Inc., META



has shifted its technology focus toward artificial intelligence products after expanding its capabilities through major talent and infrastructure investments. The company completed a $14.3 billion agreement involving Scale AI employees in 2025, including the appointment of Alexandr Wang as chief AI officer. The move placed AI development at the center of Meta’s product strategy. Meta has shifted its technology focus toward artificial intelligence products after expanding its capabilities through major talent and infrastructure investments. The company completed a $14.3 billion agreement involving Scale AI employees in 2025, including the appointment of Alexandr Wang as chief AI officer. The move placed AI development at the center of Meta’s product strategy.

Meta’s recent gains also followed strong interest in its latest AI offerings and announcements at Meta Connect. The company introduced new AI-powered products, including the Muse Charm device and updates to its personal AI platform. These developments increased attention around Meta’s broader push into consumer AI services.

Meta Expands AI Product Strategy With New Devices and Platforms

Meta presented its personal superintelligence strategy through new hardware and software products during Meta Connect. The company introduced lightweight spatial computing glasses designed with advanced display technology and AI interaction features. The device weighs about 100 grams and includes eye and hand tracking capabilities.

Meta expanded its smart eyewear lineup with the third-generation Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3 glasses. The company also introduced Ray-Ban Meta Audio glasses that focus on open-ear listening and voice-based AI interaction. These products build on Meta’s existing partnership with Ray-Ban maker EssilorLuxottica.

Meta highlighted the growth of its Muse AI agent following its recent launch. Data from Sensor Tower showed that Muse recorded 2.8 million downloads across the United States and Canada App Stores within its first 12 days. The platform recorded higher early downloads than ChatGPT during the same period.

Meta AI Momentum Supports Market Capitalization Growth

Meta’s stock performance reflected strong market activity during the week as the company gained approximately $234 billion in market capitalization. The increase came as the company showcased new AI products and expanded its consumer technology ecosystem. Meta shares continued trading near recent highs following the announcements.

The company has invested heavily in AI research, computing infrastructure, and product development to strengthen its position in the technology sector. Meta’s AI strategy includes integrating intelligent features across its social media platforms, devices, and digital services. The approach connects AI development with its broader product ecosystem.

Meta continues developing hardware products that combine artificial intelligence with everyday consumer experiences. The company’s latest announcements include improvements to smart glasses, voice interaction, and spatial computing. data.full_text:
Meta Platforms CEO Mark Zuckerberg claims personal superintelligence is within reach

Zuckerberg's vision for AI that knows you better than you know yourself is backed by $145 billion in capital spending and a 49% stake in Scale AI

by Editorial Team 14 minutes ago

Mark Zuckerberg wants to give every person on Earth their own superintelligent AI. Not sell it. Give it away, or close to it. In a roughly 6,500-word essay published on August 10, titled “The Future Is for Everyone: The Path to a Positive AI Future,” the Meta Platforms CEO laid out a vision where billions of people and small businesses gain access to personal superintelligence, powered by open-source models, running across devices from phones to smart glasses. The $145 billion bet Meta’s 2026 capital spending budget stands at $145 billion, with the bulk flowing into data centers and AI infrastructure. A significant chunk of that strategic commitment materialized through Meta’s $14.3 billion acquisition of a 49% stake in Scale AI, the data-labeling and AI infrastructure company. That deal also birthed Meta Superintelligence Labs, a new division led by Scale AI CEO Alexandr Wang. The groundwork was visible as far back as July 30, 2025, when Zuckerberg published a letter declaring that developing superintelligence was “now in sight.” The August essay expanded that claim into a full thesis: personal superintelligence isn’t just possible, it’s the morally correct path forward. What “personal superintelligence” actually means Zuckerberg’s version of superintelligence isn’t the sci-fi scenario where one omniscient AI sits in a government bunker making decisions for humanity. His pitch is closer to a hyper-capable personal assistant that deeply understands your goals, preferences, and context, then acts on them across every device you own. The AI would live on your Meta smart glasses, your phone, your laptop, and would be, in Zuckerberg’s framing, working for you rather than for a centralized institution. AI, tech, and the markets they move—in one daily briefing. Daily. Free. Join 34,000+ readers across crypto, finance, and policy. We respect your privacy. Unsubscribe anytime. The essay draws a sharp line between Meta’s approach and what Zuckerberg characterizes as the competition’s model: tightly controlled AI systems developed behind closed doors by a small number of powerful organizations. His argument is that concentrating superintelligent capabilities in the hands of a few entities creates risks that outweigh the dangers of broad distribution. Open-source is the vehicle for this philosophy. By releasing models that anyone can inspect, modify, and deploy, Meta positions itself as the populist alternative in an industry increasingly defined by access gates and API pricing tiers. The distributed power argument Zuckerberg’s essay repeatedly returns to a core thesis: distributed power is safer than centralized control. His logic: when power is distributed, no single actor can cause catastrophic damage, and the collective wisdom of billions of users creates a natural check on misuse. What this means for the competitive landscape Meta’s strategy creates an interesting dynamic in the AI race. OpenAI, Google DeepMind, and Anthropic have all pursued models where access is mediated through APIs, subscriptions, and enterprise contracts. Meta is essentially saying: we’ll build something just as powerful and hand it out. The $14.3 billion Scale AI investment signals that Meta isn’t just talking. Alexandr Wang, who built Scale AI into one of the most important data infrastructure companies in the AI ecosystem, now runs a lab with a singular mandate: build superintelligence and distribute it.

23일 IT 업계에 따르면 메타의 뮤즈가 지난 8일 출시 열흘 만에 미국 애플 앱스토어 무료 앱 다운로드 순위에서 챗GPT를 제치고 1위에 올랐다. 당시 메타 주가도 전 거래일보다 10% 넘게 급등했다.
뮤즈는 이용자 요청에 따라 쇼핑과 여행 예약, 이메일 발송 등을 처리하는 AI 에이전트다. 전용 앱과 왓츠앱을 통해 이용할 수 있어 이용자 취향과 과거 대화를 기억해 작업을 돕는다. 결제나 이메일 발송처럼 중요한 작업을 실행할 때는 이용자 승인을 받는다.
뮤즈 흥행에 주식시장도 반응했다. 지난 21일 메타 주가는 전 거래일보다 11.4% 급등했고, 시가총액은 하루 만에 1923억 달러(약 261조 2500억원) 늘었다. 웰스파고는 메타 목표주가를 기존 640달러에서 796달러(약 108만 1400원)로 상향 조정했다. 뮤즈가 광고 외 수익원을 확보하는 계기가 될 수 있다는 기대가 주가를 끌어올린 것이다.
뮤즈는 메타가 지난해부터 추진해온 AI 조직 개편과 투자 성과를 가늠할 주요 서비스로 평가받고 있다. 메타는 지난해 6월 '메타 초지능연구소(Meta Superintelligence Labs·MSL)'를 출범시키고 차세대 AI 연구와 제품 개발 체계를 재편했다.
당시 메타는 스케일AI 창업자인 알렉산더 왕을 연구소 최고AI책임자로 영입했으며, 냇 프리드먼 전 깃허브 최고경영자(CEO)에게 AI 제품과 응용 연구를 맡겼다. 같은 달 스케일AI에 143억 달러를 투자하고 오픈AI·구글·앤트로픽 출신 연구자들을 영입하는 등 인재 확보에도 공을 들였다.
그동안 마크 저커버그 메타 CEO가 내세운 사업 방향은 이용자 개개인 목표와 상황을 이해하고 일상 업무를 돕는 ‘개인 초지능’이다. 뮤즈는 이 구상을 소비자용 서비스로 구현한 사례다. 메타는 무료 서비스와 함께 월 20달러·100달러 구독 상품을 마련했으며, 향후 스마트 안경에도 뮤즈를 적용할 계획이다.
다수 외신은 메타가 뮤즈를 외부 서비스와 연동하는 방향을 사업 확장 수단으로 보고 있다. 메타는 최근 기업과 개발자가 뮤즈에 서비스를 연결할 수 있는 플랫폼을 개방했으며, 쇼피파이는 뮤즈에서 ‘숍 페이’를 이용한 쇼핑을 지원한다고 발표했다. 이용자가 뮤즈를 통해 상품을 찾고 구매하는 흐름이 확산하면 메타가 소비자와 기업을 연결하는 새로운 거래 접점을 확보할 수 있다.
업계에선 뮤즈 이용자 신뢰 확보가 필요하다는 의견도 나오고 있다. 아마존은 뮤즈의 자사 쇼핑몰 접근을 승인하지 않았다며 메타에 해당 기능에서 아마존을 제외해달라고 요청한 바 있다. 개인정보 접근과 작업 실행을 수반하는 만큼 보안과 오작동 우려를 해소하는 것도 과제인 것으로 전해졌다.
비즈니스인사이더는 "메타가 초기 다운로드 열기를 지속적인 이용과 유료 구독으로 연결할 수 있다면, 초지능연구소와 인프라에 쏟아부은 투자를 사업 성과로 입증하는 계기가 될 전망"이라고 분석했다.

data.title: Muse登顶，Meta靠agent扳回一局
data.ai_summary: On September 23, 2026, Muse topped the US App Store's free app chart 10 days after launch, surpassing ChatGPT. Manus announced a $500 million financing round at a $4 billion valuation. Meta's shift to personal agents, leveraging its social ecosystem, offers a new competitive path.

industries.name: Agents & Autonomous Workflows (Tool Use, Planning, Multi-Agent)

data.full_text: Muse reaches the top, Meta recovers a game with agents. On September 23, 2026, Muse topped the US App Store's free app chart just 10 days after its launch, surpassing ChatGPT. Almost at the same time, another representative product on the personal agent route, Manus, also announced a new round of financing, planning to raise $500 million with an estimated valuation of about $4 billion. Agents are providing a path for leading AI companies to 'overtake on a curve.' While foundational models are important, in the agent's arena, product design, tool invocation, task execution, permission management, and user entry have also joined the battlefield. Latecomers do not necessarily have to win over OpenAI and Anthropic on the model leaderboard first; they also have the opportunity to achieve results at the application level. Meta has clearly embarked on this 'shortcut.' Over the past year, it has not had an easy time catching up in the model competition. A lot of money has been spent, many people have been recruited, and computing power has been piled up, but the results that ordinary users can perceive have been relatively limited. Until Muse, Meta finally had a true AI blockbuster of its own. 01 What makes Muse a blockbuster? When Muse was just released, its functions were not particularly special. It can browse the web, invoke tools, process files, and help users book hotels, send emails, and shop. These capabilities have already been demonstrated by ChatGPT, Claude, and even the previous Manus. Logically, these functions are likely to encounter privacy and permission boundaries, making it difficult for users not to worry about the security risks of agents. If you let it organize your schedule, you have to open your calendar; if you let it read your emails, it has to access your inbox; if you let it help you shop, it not only needs to know your address and preferences but also needs to access your account and payment information. Prompt injection is also something to be cautious about. When agents browse the web, read emails, and files, they constantly come into contact with information from the outside world. If someone hides a malicious command in a webpage, enticing the model to send out user data, an agent with high permissions may pass the attack all the way to the real account. Meta admitted while developing Muse that no matter how well the model is trained, agents will make mistakes and can be attacked. Its uniqueness lies in the fact that it does not rely entirely on the model being obedient for security; instead, it has built a complete permission system outside the model. In simple terms, Muse provides each user with an independent computer in the cloud. You can think of it as a remote computer (virtual machine) that is always on and belongs only to you, equipped with a browser, capable of storing files and running programs. Muse checks information, processes files, and runs tasks, all of which are completed on this computer. Your files, web login status, email, and calendar connections will not mix with other users. Even if Muse needs to work for you long-term, it operates within this independent computer, preventing it from running around the entire system with permissions. It is worth noting that Muse, residing in this computer, is not the true 'administrator' of this computer. Meta has divided the entire system into two mutually isolated security zones, with Muse residing in one zone and the other housing truly sensitive items—such as user login credentials, security services, and an independent security agent named Sentinel. This Sentinel is specifically responsible for approving network access and third-party services. Muse can request to send emails or invoke accounts, but the actual approval comes from Sentinel. It can check which website Muse is preparing to access, which address, what request method is being used, and what content is being sent out. Passwords and payment information follow a similar logic. Login credentials are stored in an independent secure storage; Muse can use them but cannot see the specific content; sensitive operations like sending emails or purchasing items will require user confirmation again. Users can also specify the permissions of a particular connector, such as whether the email is only allowed to read or if sending is also permitted. The payment process adds another layer of isolation; after Muse integrates with Stripe's Link, it can generate a one-time payment card, preventing the actual bank card information from being directly exposed to the agent or merchants. Layered protections limit the potential damage Muse could cause. Users are willing to trust it—or rather, willing to believe that even if something goes wrong, it won't cause much trouble—only then does it have the opportunity to truly enter the lives of ordinary people. Of course, just being secure is not enough. The model behind Muse is Meta's self-developed Muse Spark. Alexandr Wang later revealed that from Muse Spark 1 to the latest 1.3, this entire model series has been preparing for Muse as a personal agent from the very beginning, with each upgrade focusing on strengthening agent and multimodal capabilities. Beyond the model, Muse is backed by Meta's entire product ecosystem. It can connect to platforms like Instagram and Facebook and can also be used directly in WhatsApp. The official case provided by Meta is that if you are preparing to invite friends over for dinner, Muse can browse the recipe short videos you have saved on Instagram, help you choose dishes, create a shopping list, and remember if your friends have any dietary restrictions, and finally help you send out the invitations. Axios specifically mentioned that Muse's rapid rise to fame relies not only on the model itself but also on several things Meta has always excelled at—turning complex technology into products that ordinary people can use, quickly pushing products to a large number of users, and understanding what users really like and need. About 10 days after its launch, Muse surged to the top of the US App Store's free iPhone app chart, surpassing ChatGPT. Meta's grand AI reconstruction over the past year has finally produced a result that ordinary users can directly perceive. 02 No longer obsessed with SOTA, Meta aims at personal agents. Over the past year, Meta's position among leading AI companies has been somewhat awkward. A lot of money has been spent, many people have been recruited, and computing power has been increasingly piled up. However, compared to OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google, Meta has always fallen a bit short—let's not mention the first two; Google at least has cloud services and the TPU ecosystem to support its AI landscape. In contrast, Meta has yet to produce a sufficiently convincing big result. In 2025, Llama 4 was disappointing, and the originally highly anticipated Behemoth has also been repeatedly delayed. Once riding a wave of open-source, Meta has gradually fallen behind in the SOTA model competition. Thus, Meta began its reconstruction work. In June 2025, it spent $14.3 billion to acquire 49% of Scale AI, directly bringing in Alexandr Wang to lead the new AI system; subsequently, it established Meta Superintelligence Labs (referred to as MSL), offering exorbitant salaries in the hundreds of millions to recruit talent from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google DeepMind, with the AI organization undergoing multiple reorganizations within six months. Computing power has also been ramped up, with Meta's capital expenditure reaching $72.2 billion in 2025, and guidance for 2026 further raised to $130 billion to $145 billion, along with the construction of gigawatt-level AI data centers like Prometheus and Hyperion. By April of this year, Muse Spark was released. Meta itself stated that this was the first model output from MSL 'after rebuilding the AI technology stack from scratch' for nine months. We can view Manus as an important inspiration for Meta's shift towards agents. In December last year, Meta briefly acquired Manus, which is most famous for combining models, browsers, tools, and execution environments into a general agent capable of completing complex tasks independently. However, this transaction of over $2 billion was later required by regulators to be dismantled, but Meta's willingness to spend such a large sum on Manus already indicates that it at least believes this path is worth trying. Meta could not retain Manus but has retained the agent logic represented by Manus. Coincidentally, Manus itself later began to move towards personal agents. In February, it integrated its product into Telegram, with the official documentation stating: 'Your personal agent, anytime, anywhere.' Agents are the entry point for tasks; ideally, users only need to provide their needs, and the agent can complete the tasks—users do not need to think about which model or tool is being used in the middle. Meta has not given up on training models, but it no longer waits for the model to take the lead before considering how to develop the product. Models are starting to become the foundation, while agents are becoming a more direct breakthrough. The Muse Spark series of models is precisely aimed at personal agents; and the Muse product has proven that this path can indeed yield very impressive results. This route is not niche; it is even full of opportunities. Besides Muse, a personal agent called Instinct has already been chased by capital even before its official full launch. It is still in the invitation testing phase, capable of integrating email, messages, calendars, and locations, helping users shop, book restaurants, cancel subscriptions, and has recently begun testing independent email and call capabilities. At the end of August, it completed financing at an estimated valuation of about $2.5 billion; in September, according to The Information, the company is discussing refinancing $1 billion, with its valuation directly soaring to about $10 billion. 03 'Choice is greater than effort.' If we zoom out a bit more, we can see that several old tech giants that once chased large models have now begun to go their separate ways. Google is one of the few companies still insisting on a full-stack approach: competing for models, developing agents, selling cloud services, and even manufacturing its own chips. Earlier, there were rumors that Google might withdraw from the top model competition, but just in the past few days, an unusually capable model named 'gemini-3.8-flash' appeared in the Arena, widely speculated by the community to be the unreleased Gemini 4 Pro. On the other hand, the Flash series has been updated almost every three weeks, with Google releasing Gemini 3.8 Live and 3.8 Live Extended Thinking in September. At this year's I/O, Google directly announced its entry into the 'Search Agent era,' allowing agents to track information for users 24/7; Google Cloud also launched the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform. At the foundational level, there is already the eighth generation of TPU, Google Cloud, and the entire AI infrastructure. Microsoft's and Amazon's choices are quite different; they are concentrating their advantages on enterprise services and AI infrastructure. Although Microsoft is still working on the MAI series and Amazon has Nova, models are no longer the primary goal for these two companies. Microsoft now emphasizes a multi-model platform. Azure AI Foundry provides OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI, and Microsoft's own MAI models simultaneously, allowing enterprises to choose freely based on quality, cost, and tasks. Microsoft's latest financial report disclosed that the number of customers using multiple models has increased fivefold this year; Foundry and Agent 365 are responsible for integrating these models into enterprise data, permissions, and agent systems. Rather than striving to make its own model the strongest, Microsoft wants to ensure that regardless of which model is better in the end, enterprises are using Azure. Amazon's shift is even more apparent. In July this year, Amazon directly laid off some positions in its AGI team. Previously, this relatively independent AGI organization had been merged into a larger technology department, alongside chips and quantum computing; several core leaders, including Rohit Prasad and David Luan, have also left one after another. Amazon's explanation is to streamline priorities and concentrate resources on areas that can create the most value for customers. Meanwhile, AWS is increasingly emphasizing Bedrock and AgentCore. Bedrock directly integrates OpenAI models, Codex, and hosted agents; AgentCore is even explicitly designed to be 'model-agnostic,' allowing developers to switch models freely, with AWS responsible for the runtime environment, permissions, security, and monitoring. Its approach is similar to Microsoft's; rather than spending a lot of effort chasing SOTA, it is better to ensure that models and agents developed by others ultimately run on AWS. Meta is taking a third path. Although Meta is also building giant data centers and this year has even been reported to plan to sell some AI computing power externally, compared to Google, Microsoft, and Amazon, Meta does not have a mature public cloud business to directly meet AI demands. Meta's existing advantages lie on the other end, in the billions of ordinary users, social relationships, content recommendations, advertising systems, and consumer-grade entry points like Instagram, Facebook, WhatsApp, and Threads. In the SOTA model competition, these things are almost useless; however, once the competition shifts to personal agents, the situation changes completely. A truly useful personal agent not only needs a sufficiently intelligent model but also needs to know what you like, who you interact with, and what you are planning to do; it must be able to access the software you use daily and have a way to stay by your side long-term. At this point, the 'old business' that Meta has accumulated suddenly becomes part of its AI capabilities. Social relationships become context, content recommendations become an understanding of user interests, billions of users become distribution channels, and WhatsApp and glasses can continue to serve as entry points. The real importance of Muse lies here. At least from the start of Muse, Meta is no longer just proving that it still sits at the forefront of AI with 'money, cards, and people.' It has a truly table-worthy result, and this result was not obtained by copying the methods that OpenAI excels at. Meta has finally found a battlefield that suits its strengths. In fact, the three major domestic companies have also set their sights on the direction of personal agents. Tencent, ByteDance, and Alibaba each have different inherent advantages and have recently taken similar actions. Unlike office agents that are more workflow-oriented, personal agents are meant to take over a person's daily life. In this battlefield, Tencent's strongest assets are relationships and services. WeChat has interpersonal relationships, chat, payment, mini-programs, public accounts, video accounts, and a large number of offline services; if a personal agent is to truly handle users' life affairs, WeChat is almost a natural operating platform. The recently gray-scaled WeChat assistant 'Xiao Wei' has already begun to call native WeChat functions and mini-programs to handle tasks for users. ByteDance's strengths lie in content, recommendations, and consumer-facing AI entry points. Douyin knows what users like, Doubao already has a large user base, and Feishu has a grasp of work context; the latest Doubao mobile assistant has further entered the system layer, starting to directly operate the phone and complete tasks across applications. Alibaba's advantages are in transactions and commercial services. Taobao, Tmall, Alipay, Ele.me, Gaode, Feizhu, DingTalk, along with Alibaba Cloud, cover shopping, payment, local life, travel, and work. Qianwen has already begun to connect these services, allowing AI to directly complete searches, orders, payments, and travel planning; Ant's Ahfu is also trying to manage users' personal health information from a health scenario. In this direction, it may not be so important who can create the largest personal agent. As long as several major companies start competing to handle tasks for users, ultimately, it is still us who benefit.

data.title: INOD Stock Rallies After Hunterbrook Ties Firm To Meta’s Muse, Reveals Long Position
data.ai_summary: Shares of Innodata Inc. rose nearly 15% after Hunterbrook said the firm may be training Meta's Muse assistant, with a long position disclosed. Hunterbrook estimated Meta as Innodata's largest customer, accounting for about $146 million, or 58% of 2025 sales. Neither company confirmed the claim.
data.author: Stocktwits Inc

industries.name: Data, Analytics & AI Training (BI, Data Engineering, ML/GenAI)

data.full_text:
Advertisement|Remove ads.
Shares of Innodata Inc. (INOD) jumped nearly 15% on Tuesday, marking its best day since mid-May, after a Hunterbrook research note said the data company may be helping train Meta’s new Muse assistant.
Hunterbrook Media’s affiliate, Hunterbrook Capital, further disclosed it was long the stock. INOD closed at $69.97, up $8.92, after trading as high as $74.93. Shares edged up another 2% after hours as well.
Hunterbrook said former employees and job listings point to Meta as Innodata’s largest customer. It estimated that account was about $146 million, or 58% of 2025 sales. The firm said Innodata recently described work for that client on “personalization of long-horizon agents”—training software that can remember preferences and finish multi-step tasks, not just answer questions. That description, Hunterbrook argued, lines up with Muse.
Neither company confirmed it to Hunterbrook. Innodata further did not respond to Stocktwits’s request for comment on the report.
Meta launched Muse on Sept. 8 as a consumer agent that can browse the web, handle mail and calendars, and carry out errands. Within about 10 days, it reached No. 1 among free iPhone apps in the United States, Hunterbrook noted, with a 4.9-star rating. Outside trackers later put early downloads in the millions and said Muse briefly passed ChatGPT on Apple’s U.S. free chart.
Innodata sells training data and human review to AI builders. The stock had come down from a June high near $121.50 as investors feared Meta might pull work inside after taking a large stake in Scale AI. Hunterbrook said a former Innodata employee told it that the opposite had happened so far.
Innodata’s second quarter showed some mix shift: the top customer fell to 37% of revenue from 56% in Q1, while a second big-tech account rose to 34%. Quarterly sales were $92.1 million, up 58% from a year earlier.
On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around INOD stock jumped from ‘bullish’ to ‘extremely bullish’ over the past 24 hours, while message volume increased from ‘high’ to ‘extremely high’ levels.
A Stocktwits user voiced optimism for a further rally on Wednesday if more details emerge. “Innodata can really ramp revenues with MUSE growth!” they wrote.
Another report said the news is unconfirmed and speculative but added that most big tech indeed use the firm and there is no reason Meta wouldn’t.
INOD stock has gained 37% year-to-date.
